key_verse.text: But whosoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

cards.title: It was necessary.
cards.narrative:
Jews went around Samaria. Centuries of contempt between two peoples who had once been one. Days of detour rather than set foot on that land.

Jesus did not go around.

There was a woman at a well who did not yet know she was being sought.

verse_overlay.text: And he must needs go through Samaria.

cards.revelation_key: Jesus rerouted His journey around a woman the world had stopped searching for.

cards.title: Jacob's well. The sixth hour.
cards.narrative:
Tired from the road. Alone at the well.

The sixth hour — the midday sun.

The same hour she would come.

verse_overlay.text: Then came he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph. Now Jacob's well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.

cards.revelation_key: The place was not coincidence. The hour was not coincidence. He was never there by accident.

cards.verse_text: There came a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus said unto her, Give me to drink. (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy food.) Then said the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that you, being a Jew, ask drink of me, who am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
cards.reflection:
Women went to the well in the morning. Together. She came at noon. Alone.

That is not a minor detail. It is her entire story in a single decision.

And the first to speak to her did not judge her. Did not ignore her. He asked her for something.

The Son of God made Himself vulnerable before her before she knew His name.

That is how grace enters. Not with power. With humility.
cards.revelation_key: Jesus spoke first. To her. In the place where she had learned to be invisible.

cards.title: Two Kinds of Thirst
cards.subtitle: She was talking about water. He was talking about something more.
cards.content:
Jesus offered living water. She heard it practically: spring water, flowing water, water you don't have to come and fetch at midday under the sun.

But He was pointing at the well. At the rope. At everything she had carried there every day.

Never. Not for a long time. Never — that's what Jesus promised her.

💧 Jacob's well was real. It was history. It was a heritage of centuries. Jesus does not ignore it. But what He offers does not come from outside. It comes from within. It is not a spring you must return to. It is a fountain that rises up inside the one who receives it.

She recognized it herself, even without fully understanding — and asked for exactly that water.

She was still thinking about a well.

But she was leaning toward Him. And that was enough.
cards.revelation_key: Sometimes our thirst points us to Jesus before our understanding does.

scripture_connections.text: Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinks of this water shall thirst again: But whosoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
The woman said unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come here to draw.
Ho, everyone that thirsts, come you to the waters, and he that has no money; come you, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.

cards.title: Jesus said unto her, Go, call your husband, and come here.
cards.narrative: She answered with the most honest thing she had ever said at that well.

verse_overlay.text: Jesus said unto her, Go, call your husband, and come here. The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, You have well said, I have no husband: For you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband: that said you truly.

cards.revelation_key: He knew her completely. And He said: you have spoken truly.

cards.title: You have well said.
cards.subtitle: What Jesus did not say
cards.content:
He did not say: you are broken.
He did not say: you should be ashamed.
He did not say: fix yourself before we speak.

He said: you have well said.

He praised her honesty in the very moment He revealed what she was carrying.

Five husbands. Five wells. Five attempts to quench a thirst none of them could touch.

He did not mention her past to shame her. He mentioned it to show her He knew her — and stayed.

That is the difference between the world and Jesus. The world exposes to shame. Jesus reveals to set free.

She came to hide. He came to find her.
cards.revelation_key: Jesus knew every well she had been to. And He did not move.

cards.title: Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet.
cards.narrative:
Something inside her was moving.

Not evasion. Recognition. Her spirit was sensing that she was not speaking with an ordinary person.

The fear, the curiosity, something awakening within her, led her to ask the oldest question between her people and the Jews. Not to escape. To understand.

verse_overlay.text: The woman said unto him, Sir, I perceive that you are a prophet. Our fathers worshiped in this mountain; and you say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.

cards.revelation_key: Before she knew who He was, her spirit was already recognizing Him.

cards.title: In spirit and in truth.
cards.subtitle: An answer larger than the question.
cards.content:
Jesus did not dodge her question. He answered it completely.

But He took her further than she expected — explaining that true worship was never about geography to begin with.

Not a mountain. Not a temple. Not a correct location.

A relationship. Interior. True.

She had come with a question about places. He was speaking to her about the heart.
cards.revelation_key: She asked where to worship. He showed her how.

scripture_connections.text: Jesus said unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour comes, when you shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. You worship you know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews. But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeks such to worship him. God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
But the hour comes, and now is, when the true worshipers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeks such to worship him.

cards.verse_text: The woman said unto him, I know that Messiah comes, who is called Christ: when he comes, he will tell us all things. Jesus said unto her, I that speak unto you am he.
cards.reflection:
Throughout the Gospel of John, Jesus does not directly announce who He is. He speaks in signs, in images, in declarations that require discernment.

Here, beside a well in Samaria, at noon, He says it plainly.

And He says it to her.

Not to a Levite priest, nor a Pharisee, nor a disciple.

But to the woman who came alone — ashamed, humbled.

She went from asking whether Jesus was greater than Jacob, a patriarch of the past, to receiving the declaration of the Messiah, the living hope. In a single conversation beside that well.
cards.revelation_key: The first person to receive this powerful declaration was the last person the world would have expected. That is how God works.

cards.title: The woman then left her waterpot.
cards.narrative:
The disciples arrived. They marveled that He was talking with a woman. None of them asked anything.

And she made a decision.

verse_overlay.text: And upon this came his disciples, and marveled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seek you? or, Why talk you with her? The woman then left her water pot, and went her way into the city, and said to the men, Come, see a man, who told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?

cards.revelation_key: She did not forget the waterpot. She was transformed. The water she had come for was no longer enough.

cards.title: The waterpot she left behind.
cards.subtitle: What an abandoned waterpot means.
cards.content:
In the previous encounter we saw Bartimaeus throw down his cloak before receiving his healing — faith that lets go before having anything to hold onto.

She left her waterpot after the encounter. What Jesus placed inside her had already made small what she carried in her hands.

Two people. Two abandoned objects. The same Jesus.

But there is something more in what she did.

🪣 In the Greek, the question she brought to the city is framed with a word that anticipates uncertainty: Is not this the Christ?

She did not arrive proclaiming. She arrived inviting. She knew that a woman with her history would not be believed if she made a declaration. So she wrapped the revelation in a question that compelled each person to go and see for themselves.

That was not naivety. That was wisdom.

And it worked.
cards.revelation_key: She brought her wound as her testimony. And an entire city came out to see.

scripture_connections.text: Then they went out of the city, and came unto him.

And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for you: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather boast in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

cards.title: And many believed.
cards.subtitle: Because of the word of the woman.
cards.content:
We must understand what this means.

In the first century, a woman had no public voice. A Samaritan woman with her history had even less. The men of that city had no cultural or social reason to listen to her.

And they went out.

That is not normal. That is supernatural — many believed because of her testimony.

John — a first-century Jewish writer formed in that culture — recorded that it was this woman who brought an entire city to the Messiah. That cannot be explained apart from the Holy Spirit.

Even more believed once they heard Jesus themselves.

She arrived alone. She left as a movement.
She arrived carrying shame. She left with a testimony.
She arrived to hide. She left to find others.

That is what Jesus does. In our imperfection He loves us, transforms us, and uses us.
cards.revelation_key: God took the person the world disqualified and made her the first evangelist of Samaria.

scripture_connections.text: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, who testified, He told me all that ever I did.

And many more believed because of his own word; And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of your saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.

cards.title: The well at dusk.
cards.narrative:
The same well. The same place.

But the waterpot is gone. Only the rope curled over the edge.

Something happened here.

verse_overlay.text: And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of your saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.

cards.revelation_key: An encounter with Jesus always leaves something different in the place where it occurred.

cards.title: Your encounter
cards.subtitle: What well do you keep coming back to?

discovery_questions.question: She returned to the same well every day. What have you kept returning to, hoping this time it would be different? What are you really looking for in that place?
Jesus knew everything about her and stayed. Is there something in your story you believe would push Jesus away if He knew it? What would it mean to know He already knows — and is still here?
She left the waterpot because something inside her changed. What are you carrying that Jesus is inviting you to leave at the well?
She did not wait until everything was settled. She went with what she had: her story and a question. Who needs to hear what Jesus has done in your life — just as you are, today?

prayer.title: Prayer of the one who came alone at noon
prayer.content:
Lord Jesus, I come to this well.

Not because I have it figured out. Not because my story is clean. I come because I am thirsty and I have tried other places.

You know everything about me. Every well I have returned to. Every time I looked in the wrong place for what only You can give.

And You are still here. Not to expose me. To find me.

Like her, I want the encounter that changes what I carry. That what came in as thirst, goes out as testimony.

Transform me. Use me. In my imperfection, in my story, in what I am.

Give me the water that never runs dry. And give me the courage to leave my waterpot.

In Jesus' name, amen.

completion_verse.text: The woman then left her water pot, and went her way into the city, and said to the men, Come, see a man, who told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?

cards.reflection_prompt: What is the waterpot you need to leave behind today? And who needs to hear your 'come and see'?
